River MillValues
Our school values are at the core of everything we do. They underpin our teaching and learning and characterise the culture of our school.
We Share, We Try Our Best, We Are Respectful, We Are Good Friends, We Are Kind.

Noticeboard
The Parent Teacher Association (PTA) at River Mill exists to promote positive relationships between staff, parents and the school community. It aims to support the school by raising money for additional facilities that do not come from government funding.
We are currently raising funds for: an outdoor reading gazebo/shed, more reading books for class libraries, additional large play equipment and resources for our school allotment.
Every River Mill parent/carer is automatically a member of the PTA - everyone is welcome.
We run many events throughout the year – our first event is the Easter Egg-stravaganza on 29th March.
For more information please look under the parent tab/PTA.
In order to be kept updated about PTA events and activities you must sign up to our mailing list - just send an email to pta@rivermillprimaryschool.co.uk to sign up.
Welcome
The aim of our website is to keep you informed about what is going on at River Mill, how we work and share what is important to use as a school community.
The children at River Mill are motivated, happy and enthusiastic about learning and growing together as a community. It is important to us that we give all children the best possible start in life. We aim to develop strong relationships with parents to ensure that we achieve this. We welcome visitors, please make an appointment to visit us and see for yourself what makes our school community so special.
Suzanne Leader - Head Teacher

pageCache.pageTitle: River Mill Primary School - Breakfast & After School Club
pageCache.text:
Breakfast & After School Club
We run a Breakfast and After School Club (BASC) on site, staffed by River Mill staff, providing high quality out of hours care for River Mill children during term time. Applications for BASC must be made on line using the form below, and in the event that the club is over-subscribed, we will maintain a waiting list for places. Full details are contained in our BASC policy.
To see River Mill's Breakfast and After School Club Admissions and Fees Policy, please click here.
To see the Breakfast and After School Club information booklet, please click here.
To see the Breakfast and After School Club menu, please click here.
To see the Breakfast and After School Club allergen menu, please click here.
Our breakfast club is open from 7.30 each morning offering your children a wide and varied breakfast menu which includes toast, cereals, fruit as well as extras such as pancakes and crumpets on a rota basis. They will also have the opportunity to play with toys, games, craft and physical activities.
Our after school club runs from the end of school until 6.00 pm and includes a light evening meal. On arrival the children have the opportunity to participate in a wide range of activities. On occasions we will also invite external providers in to run additional activities for children.
If you would like your child to attend our Breakfast and After School Club please complete the Expression of Interest form below. The club manager will then contact you to let you know if there are any spaces or add your details to the waiting list.

pageCache.pageTitle: River Mill Primary School - Junior Road Safety Officers
pageCache.text:
Junior Road Safety Officers
Welcome back everyone!
It’s the final term of school and although the sun hasn’t yet arrived lots of you have been walking, cycling or scooting to school, so well done!
Thank you to all of those children who took part in Walk to School Week last half term. I hope you enjoyed all the activities in class but most importantly made the most of being out in the fresh with your friends and families.
A huge well done to Jeremy and Steven who stood up in assembly in front of the whole school and helped me deliver the PowerPoint! They were clear, confident and very professional! Well done boys!
Thank you also to Mr Jordan and the Eco Council who created posters for us to help promote Walk to School Week, some fantastic designs!
We will be giving out certificates to those children who managed to walk to school everyday during Walk to School Week.
And Steven and Jeremy will also be looking through the latest competitions to ‘design a new shoe’ and we will announce the winners soon.
As always, a polite reminder to be safe and considerate when parking in the car park.
But remember you can no longer do this in September. Hopefully this will positively impact the ways in which our families travel to school!
Miss Cole and the JRSO’s.

pageCache.pageTitle: River Mill Primary School - Character Education
pageCache.text:
Character Education
Character Education at River Mill
Character Education is a fundamental part of our curriculum at River Mill. We believe that developing the 'whole child' and that children will leave us in Year 6 as well-rounded individuals who demonstrate a range of positive character strengths is a very important part of primary education.
At River Mill we have developed a list of those characteristics we feel are the most important to teach. Our curriculum is infused with opportunities for children to develop their character strengths and virtues. These are taught and celebrated through assemblies, circle times, discrete lessons and our weekly 'Star of the Week' celebrations.
Character education includes all educational activities that help young people develop positive personal strengths called virtues. Children are encouraged to decide wisely the kind of person they wish to become and to learn to make positive choices about their behaviour. The aim of character education is to enable children to know how to choose the right course of action in different and often tricky situations, something we are sure you will also be doing all the time at home.
Each month we will focus on a different virtue and children will be encouraged to think about how they can make positive choices linked to each virtue. Children will be rewarded when they demonstrate each virtue. We would you to support us by talking to your children about the monthly virtue and thinking about why it is important. We will support you by sharing resources and activities with you under the curriculum tab – under ‘Parents’ then ‘Curriculum Education’.
Our virtue focus for January is caring
What does caring mean?
Being caring can come in many different forms, such as displaying kindness towards others, sharing with others, being polite and saying 'please' and 'thank you', being sensitive to other's feelings, showing compassion to those less fortunate and forgiving someone who has upset you.
One of the biggest reasons why this quality is so important is that it gives us the ability to help others and understand when others are in need.
Being caring allows us to make a positive difference in someone else's life.

Our School Day
Routine of the school day
We have a ‘soft start’ in the morning. This means that children can enter the school 10 minutes before the official start time from 8.40 a.m.
Morning registration is at 8.55 a.m.
The length of the school week is 32 hours and 30 minutes.
Start and end timesMorning session 8.30-12.00Mid-morning break 10.30-10.50Afternoon session 1.00-3.15
If a child misses registration they will be marked ‘Late’ (L) in the register. If they arrive after the closure of registration at 9am, they will be marked as (U) and the lateness will be recorded as an unauthorised absence for the morning session.

pageCache.pageTitle: River Mill Primary School - School Council
pageCache.text:
School Council
The School Council is an important part of school life at River Mill. The school council is a place where pupils are involved in decisions about the school that affect them. Through these meetings, all pupils have the opportunity to raise issues, share ideas and take part in discussions that involve all of their classmates. Pupils at River Mill Primary School know that this is their school and their thoughts and ideas matter. The school council allows them to reach a democratic solution.
The elections are held at the beginning of the Autumn Term. Each class chooses two representatives who agree to attend School Council meetings for a whole year in order to contribute to the improvement of the school. They feedback to their class to them know what has been discussed and decided.
The school council is managed by Miss Carley and she meets with the school councilors once a month. The councilors do a brilliant job of bringing idea/issues which are then discussed within the meeting. Our School Council aims to prepare our pupils for citizenship by teaching them about roles, rights, and responsibilities within our school community.
